subject: CFA with multiply imputed data and sampling weights

messages.author: 870a6ef52b4a0dca
messages.subject: CFA with multiply imputed data and sampling weights
parts:
I am trying to run a CFA with multiply imputed data and sampling weights (specifically using a subpopulation of my data). My code is as follows: 

mi2 = mice(df1, m = 5, maxiter = 1, where = where1)  #running imputation
imp.comp = complete(mi2, "all")   
a.out.imp = imputationList(imp.comp)  # this creates a list of the imputed datasets
designs3<-svydesign(id =~ NSCAWID, strata=~STRATUM, weights=~NANALWT3, data=a.out.imp)  #creating sampling weights
designs3_subpop = subset(designs3, subsamp == 1)  #specifying supopulation
w1subuse <- cfa(modelw1sub, ordered = TRUE, sampling.weights = designs3_subpop, data=a.out.imp) #cfa

I receive the following error:  lavaan ERROR: data= argument is not a data.fame, but of class ‘imputationList’

Any idea how I would get the CFA to run using a list of imputed datasets while also accounting for sampling weights? Any assistance would be much appreciated!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFA with multiply imputed data and sampling weights
parts:
I don't think lavaan.survey provides support for multiple imputation.  The help page suggests alternative methods:

https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan.survey/man/lavaan.survey.html

It is unfortunate that you have a stratum variable to account for, as lavaan itself can now handle weights and clustering (which would make lavaan.mi() a possibility for multiple imputations).  But I would trust Oberski's recommendations on the help page linked above.
